Not the perfect game, but one that's been in my head for a while now. Essentially the game is Third Person Action Adventure game with light Empire building mechanics set in the Neolithic Age with the ultimate goal of mastering the environment and evolving to full Homo Sapien. The Protagonist is brought into an early neolithic tribe that relies on gathering nuts and berries for food. They are in the middle of this fictitious land mass surrounded by other tribes, each of which has a historical advancement in human development. By interacting with other tribes though either conquest or diplomacy you are bringing their knowledge to your own people. Every tribe can be wiped out though violence and replace with your own peoples, or brought into your proto-civilization and increase your gene pool. Mechanically they offer the same outcome, you get whatever technology they had and acquire their land in your budding civilization.

You'd get to play though early stone tools, acquiring pottery, late stone age tools, religion, art, early horticulture, meat preservation methods, and into full on agriculture and civilization.

Gameplay would be a super tight combat system in the style of Dark Souls. Except you're fighting bobcats with a pointed stick and a rock club.

In it's original inception, the final tribe that controlled agriculture is a group of blood shamans riding dinosaurs because those fights would be insanely fun. Packing all the amazing big predators into a single game would blow realism out of the water, but spear hunting Raptors, Mammoths, Sabertooth Tigers, and Chimpanzees would be bitching.

One of the problems is I'm a huge story guy and there's inherent conflict. If there's a main character, we're talking about millions of years of human development seen though the lens of a single life time. If you play as a tribesman and each time you interact with another tribe you flash forward 500,000 years, you can't really have a cohesive story.

Then again, magic dinosaur riding shamans blow realism out of the water, so might as well have a single character.

God, so, I have a couple of ideas. This might get long.

Open-World 3rd Person Zombie Survival MMO... With a Twist!

Okay, so, everyone knows what DayZ is by now. You've probably heard of 7 Days to Die and State of Decay as well, and you should probably shoot yourself if you've never played Left 4 Dead. All awesome games, but most of them focus on one or two key areas of the apocalypse.

My idea for a game has players starting out in a small settlement. You create your character, choose your background, and you're tasked with the well being of your settlement... or you strike out on your own... or maybe you make your own settlement. Each character background would be fairly vague, but would translate to real-world skills. Mechanics, contractors, IT Techs, receptionists, etc. would all have skills that translate in some way to the apocalypse. The idea behind the gameplay is to take back cities by driving out the zombies that infest each one, building by building.

So far so good, but nothing special, right?

So you're out with your friends and the game has progressed to a point where you think you can take a smaller building on the outskirts of town. Scouts have reported little to no threat. You walk in, all cocky, when you get ambushed and bit. Here's where the real game begins.

Another part players would be playing is contributing to the cure effort in some way, be it providing samples, building facilities, or just scavenging for books, documents, antibiotics, etc. So when you get bit, you have varying degrees of success in staving off the inevitable. While it would be possible to cure yourself, it would be a pain in the butt to do so.

So the inevitable happens. You die, and your corpse is risen from it's slumber. You'd then play as a special kind of zombie, one that would 'remember' some things. Remember that background you chose? That comes into play here, too. Maybe contractors would get bonus damage to structures. Maybe electricians have a resistance to electricity and can pinpoint electrical systems for their horde. Maybe lazy people end up like boomers from L4D.

The zombies are always trying to infest new places.The goal for them is to completely eradicate the human population. They can do this through a variety of ways, including their own form of 'research' which would basically be improving the virus. Each zombie through their experiences would contribute, as they all form a hivemind of sorts.

So at the end of the day, the game might look like a slower, longer, zombie-filled game of Planetside 2. Games on a server might last a month before they reset. They might be longer or shorter. XP is shared between games, and a dead character could be revived in the next game.

There's obviously a lot of work that would go into this, but I feel like it has the potential to be an amazingly fun time if it's done right.

Multiplayer Sim City... With a Twist!

So hear me out on this one.

Games would be about 16 to 32 people. Maybe more, dunno. The idea is that each player runs a part of the government or a corporation. Every so often, players would vote among themselves on who would be mayor. Votes would get bonuses depending on various factors.

Mayor dictates the direction of the city. It would be a simple thing. "We need a new residential district." He'd set that job up, and players would compete somehow for the job. Probably like an auction system. The mayor would basically be contracting the cheapest company to do it, but would be able to see other stats of the different corps.

Corps would do various things like design transport systems, design new buildings of a few different types, and would allocate resources to run their businesses. Corps could give smaller jobs to other corps, too. So say your transportation corp needs a new HQ, they could give the job to another corp and they'd both get bonuses. However, the builder corp might sabotage the building in a small way, so that they might expand into the transport business.

It'd essentially be a competitive co-op city builder, with the mayor delegating responsibilities to corporations who are constantly trying to fuck each other over while still trying to expand and prove their worth to the city at large. It'd take a lot of balance tweaking and I have no idea how the gameplay would function in practice, but I always thought it would be a neat way to play a city builder.
